domain.name: ComfyUI & Generative Media
domain.description: Advanced ComfyUI graph architecture, identity and reference control, spatial conditioning, temporal video workflows, model adapters, environment recovery, VRAM tuning, batch automation, and reproducibility. Version-sensitive node behavior belongs in Current Intelligence.

competencies.name: Advanced Graph Architecture
competencies.description: Design large ComfyUI workflows as modular, testable systems with clear data flow and checkpoints.
competencies.purpose: Keep complex image and video workflows understandable and recoverable.

units.title: A workflow graph is a dependency graph
units.content: Models, conditioning, latents, images, masks, controls, samplers, and post steps should have explicit roles and boundaries so failures can be isolated.

units.title: Graph modularization workflow
units.content: Separate load, condition, generate, refine, composite, and export stages; group reusable branches; label checkpoints; test each branch independently; freeze working baselines before experimentation.

units.title: Graph architecture failures
units.content: Avoid giant unlabeled graphs, duplicate model loads, hidden branching assumptions, testing many variables at once, and deleting the last known-good workflow.

drills.title: Design a modular image-to-video graph
drills.prompt: Break a complex identity-preserving video workflow into reusable stages with checkpoints and failure isolation.

competencies.name: Identity & Reference Consistency
competencies.description: Combine reference images, embeddings, adapters, masks, and prompt conditioning to preserve subject identity across outputs.
competencies.purpose: Produce consistent characters or products across shots and iterations.

units.title: Identity consistency is multi-signal
units.content: Reference strength, crop, face/detail emphasis, prompt pressure, pose, seed, model family, and denoise can all affect likeness; no single control guarantees identity.

units.title: Identity-lock workflow
units.content: Choose clean references, establish a baseline still, vary one identity control at a time, lock successful settings, test pose and lighting extremes, then carry the verified stack into video or multi-shot generation.

units.title: Identity workflow failures
units.content: Avoid stacking many reference methods before measuring each one, overdriving adapters until faces distort, changing model family mid-sequence, and judging consistency from only one easy angle.

drills.title: Build an identity-lock test matrix
drills.prompt: Design a controlled test for preserving one subject across close-up, profile, wide, and motion shots.

competencies.name: Advanced Spatial Control
competencies.description: Use pose, depth, edge, segmentation, masks, and regional conditioning to control composition and geometry.
competencies.purpose: Turn generation from vague prompting into repeatable shot construction.

units.title: Control signals compete for influence
units.content: Pose, depth, edges, masks, references, and prompt conditioning can reinforce or conflict; weights and timing need deliberate coordination.

units.title: Spatial-control workflow
units.content: Define the non-negotiable geometry, choose the minimal control signal, preprocess cleanly, set influence range, add secondary controls only when needed, and inspect structure before detail refinement.

units.title: Spatial-control failures
units.content: Avoid piling multiple strong controls onto contradictory geometry, using noisy preprocessors, controlling every pixel when flexibility is useful, and blaming the sampler for bad structural guidance.

drills.title: Control a complex cinematic shot
drills.prompt: Plan pose, depth, mask, and reference controls for a character moving through a specific environment composition.

competencies.name: Video & Temporal Workflows
competencies.description: Build shot-based video generation pipelines with motion control, temporal consistency, interpolation, and post stabilization.
competencies.purpose: Generate usable motion instead of disconnected frames.

units.title: Temporal quality is more than frame quality
units.content: Identity drift, geometry drift, flicker, motion cadence, camera consistency, and transitions can fail even when individual frames look strong.

units.title: Temporal workflow
units.content: Define shot duration and motion, establish start/reference frames, choose motion guidance, generate short tests, inspect drift and cadence, refine only stable segments, then interpolate or post-process after core consistency works.

units.title: Video workflow failures
units.content: Avoid generating long clips before short tests pass, hiding identity drift with interpolation, changing too many controls between shots, and judging motion from isolated frames.

drills.title: Design a stable 5-second AI shot
drills.prompt: Create a generation and QC plan for a short character shot with camera movement and identity preservation.

competencies.name: Model, LoRA & Adapter Management
competencies.description: Track compatible checkpoints, VAEs, text encoders, LoRAs, adapters, and model-family assumptions.
competencies.purpose: Prevent silent incompatibility and make successful generations reproducible.

units.title: Model components form a compatibility stack
units.content: A checkpoint, text encoder, VAE, adapter, ControlNet, LoRA, sampler, and scheduler may have model-family assumptions that must align.

units.title: Model-stack validation
units.content: Record base family and component versions, test the base model first, add adapters one at a time, verify expected tensor/model compatibility, document weights and trigger conventions, and retain a known-good manifest.

units.title: Model-stack failures
units.content: Avoid mixing adapters from incompatible families blindly, renaming files without provenance, loading duplicate components into VRAM, and assuming a workflow shared online matches local versions.

drills.title: Build a model compatibility manifest
drills.prompt: Define the manifest FREEOS should keep for a production ComfyUI workflow using base model, VAE, LoRAs, controls, and custom nodes.

competencies.name: Custom Node Environment Recovery
competencies.description: Diagnose dependency, import, CUDA, Python, and custom-node failures without destabilizing the whole environment.

units.title: Custom nodes are executable third-party code
units.content: Installing or updating custom nodes can change Python dependencies and runtime behavior; provenance and rollback matter.

units.title: Environment recovery workflow
units.content: Capture the exact error and current versions, disable or isolate recent nodes, verify core ComfyUI, inspect dependency conflicts, test in a contained environment when possible, then reintroduce nodes incrementally.

units.title: Recovery failure modes
units.content: Avoid mass-updating every node after one failure, installing untrusted scripts blindly, mixing incompatible Python packages across environments, and deleting a working environment before exporting its manifest.

drills.title: Recover from custom-node breakage
drills.prompt: Plan isolation for ComfyUI failing after several node updates and Python dependency changes.

competencies.name: VRAM, Performance & Scheduling
competencies.description: Control model residency, precision, resolution, batching, offload, cache, and execution order for constrained GPUs.
competencies.purpose: Fit ambitious workflows into available hardware without random OOM retries.

units.title: Peak memory matters more than average memory
units.content: Multiple models, latent resolution, video frames, attention, batch size, and post-processing can overlap and push peak VRAM beyond the card even when each step fits alone.

units.title: VRAM tuning workflow
units.content: Measure baseline peak, identify resident models, reduce duplicate loads, sequence heavy stages, lower batch or resolution strategically, use supported precision/offload options, and validate quality after each change.

units.title: VRAM tuning failures
units.content: Avoid dropping every quality setting at once, treating all OOMs as leaks, keeping unused models resident, and increasing Windows pagefile as a substitute for GPU planning.

drills.title: Fit a video workflow into 8GB VRAM
drills.prompt: Design a resource plan for identity-guided video generation on an 8GB GPU.

competencies.name: Batch Automation & Reproducibility
competencies.description: Run parameter sweeps, queued jobs, API-driven workflows, metadata capture, and deterministic output organization.
competencies.purpose: Scale experiments and production without losing provenance.

units.title: An output without provenance is hard to improve
units.content: Useful production records include workflow, model stack, seeds, prompts, dimensions, control settings, node versions, and relevant environment information.

units.title: Batch experiment workflow
units.content: Define one variable or planned matrix, generate deterministic names, preserve workflow metadata, separate tests from approved outputs, score results against a rubric, and promote only verified settings into production presets.

units.title: Batch failure modes
units.content: Avoid giant undocumented sweeps, overwriting outputs, varying multiple unknowns without labeling them, and keeping only the winning image while discarding the settings that produced it.

drills.title: Design a controlled parameter sweep
drills.prompt: Plan a reproducible experiment comparing several identity and motion settings across the same shot.
